item.title: Fate Of Albion’s Old Town Hall Still Up In Air
item.description: After months of debate over the future of the former town hall on South Orange Street, the Albion Town Council voted 3-2 on Tuesday, Nov. 25 to continue exploring options for the vacant building rather than sell or demolish it.

item.title: Kosciusko Area Plan Commission Approves Rezoning Of Ag District For Robinson Construction
item.description: The Kosciusko County Area Plan Commission approved the rezoning of an agricultural district for Robinson Construction during a Wednesday, Dec. 3, meeting.

item.title: Lilly Announces Changing The Thread Collection Campaign
item.description: Eli Lilly and Co. has launched a national campaign aimed at reducing the stigma surrounding obesity, using personal stories and visual symbolism to highlight the challenges faced by people living with the disease.

item.title: Governor Braun Attends Central Midwest Carpenter Council Training Center Groundbreaking In Warsaw
item.description: Governor Mike Braun was in Warsaw for the groundbreaking for Central Midwest Carpenter Council Training Center on Wednesday, Dec. 3.

item.title: $250K Grant To Pay For Leadership Training For 50 Adults
item.description: The Orthopedics Capital Foundation, through OrthoWorx, has announce it has received a $250,000 Ignite Your Future grant from the Don Wood Foundation.

item.title: Michigan-Indiana Border Remains Blurry
item.description: Despite renewed efforts to clarify it, the roughly 110-mile boundary between Michigan and Indiana remains officially unsettled, nearly two centuries after it was last surveyed.

item.title: Harry Webb: A legacy of care in downtown Rochester
item.description: When you walk into Webb’s Pharmacy in downtown Rochester, chances are owner Harry Webb will greet you with a warm smile.
